samples.summary: The "`code` wins over prose" assertion for `isCredentialRejected` cannot fail — it passes with the code branch deleted
samples.evidence: `isCredentialRejected` (ask.mjs:600-605) checks `err.code` first and otherwise falls back to `Number(err.status)`. The test case `isCredentialRejected({ kind: "api-error", code: "USAGE_LIMIT", detail: "401" }) === false` carries NO `status`, and the fallback never reads `detail` at all — so with the whole `if (err.code) return err.code === "AUTH_REJECTED"` line removed the expression is still false (`Number(undefined)` is NaN). The comment claims it proves code precedence, but the only case that would prove it — `{ code: "USAGE_LIMIT", status: 401 }` (or `{ code: "RATE_LIMITED", status: 403 }`), which must be false — is absent from the suite. The sibling `isAccountLimit` test at ask.test.mjs:697 does this properly (code "AUTH_REJECTED" vs prose "session limit"); this one does not.

samples.evidence: The diff exports `SESSION_LIMIT_RE` from redact.mjs and imports it in ask.mjs and auth-smoke.mjs, arguing that duplicated copies drift. metrics.mjs:878 still holds the OLD literal `/\b(?:session|usage)\s+limit\b/i` (with a `code === "USAGE_LIMIT"` preference) and was neither updated nor imported from. No test in metrics.test.mjs exercises a weekly/daily/monthly limit through `classifyFixResult`/`renderFixEffort` — metrics.test.mjs:796 and :840 only use "You've hit your session limit". samples.summary: Replacing the two literal QUOTA regexes with `SESSION_LIMIT_RE` narrows matching (word boundaries), and no test covers the newly-unmatched forms
samples.evidence: `/session limit/i` and `/usage limit/i` were substring matches; `SESSION_LIMIT_RE` is `/\b(?:session|usage|weekly|daily|monthly)\s+limit\b/i`, whose trailing `\b` rejects e.g. "You have exceeded your usage limits" (plural) which previously classified as quota and now falls through to `unknown` → EXIT.auth, the exact misdiagnosis the file header warns about. auth-smoke.test.mjs adds only the weekly case (line 34) and keeps the singular "usage limit" (line 30); no plural or otherwise-suffixed form is asserted in either direction.

samples.summary: The changed pool-exhausted error (message wording, `kind`, `retryable:false`) has no test anywhere
samples.evidence: grep for `pool-exhausted` / `was retired` across scripts/ returns only ask.mjs:693-696; ask.test.mjs contains no assertion on the exhausted-pool throw at all (only token-pool.test.mjs:127 tests `isExhausted` on the pool itself). The diff rewrites the operator-facing message and argues at length about its wording, but nothing pins the message, the `kind: "pool-exhausted"` tag, or `retryable === false`, so a regression there stays green.

samples.summary: No test asserts a weekly/daily/monthly limit is non-retryable through `classifyResult` — the half of the outage the widened regex fixes in ask.mjs
samples.evidence: `classifyResult` decides `retryable` from `SESSION_LIMIT_RE.test(raw)` (ask.mjs:385). The existing pin for this property (ask.test.mjs:663-681) uses only "You've hit your session limit". The diff adds weekly/daily/monthly cases only to redact.test.mjs (classifyInfraError → code), not to the retryability path, and adds a bare-prose `isAccountLimit` weekly case; nothing asserts `classifyResult({api_error_status:429, result:"...weekly limit..."}).retryable === false` or that `isAccountLimit` accepts that classified error, which is the failover the outage narrative is about.

samples.summary: The failover loop itself is only covered through the pure `nextCredential` helper; nothing exercises askStructured retrying with the rotated credential env
samples.evidence: The behavior change (a 401/403 now rotates instead of throwing) is asserted only on `nextCredential` (ask.test.mjs:282-302) with hand-built error objects. `askStructured`'s loop (ask.mjs:708-722), including `options = { ...options, env: credentialEnv(authToken) }` on rotation, has no test with an injectable `runSession`/SDK seam, so a loop that computed `next` and failed to apply it would stay green. finding.summary: The "`code` wins over prose" assertion for `isCredentialRejected` cannot fail — it passes with the code branch deleted
finding.evidence: `isCredentialRejected` (ask.mjs:600-605) checks `err.code` first and otherwise falls back to `Number(err.status)`. The test case `isCredentialRejected({ kind: "api-error", code: "USAGE_LIMIT", detail: "401" }) === false` carries NO `status`, and the fallback never reads `detail` at all — so with the whole `if (err.code) return err.code === "AUTH_REJECTED"` line removed the expression is still false (`Number(undefined)` is NaN). The comment claims it proves code precedence, but the only case that would prove it — `{ code: "USAGE_LIMIT", status: 401 }` (or `{ code: "RATE_LIMITED", status: 403 }`), which must be false — is absent from the suite. The sibling `isAccountLimit` test at ask.test.mjs:697 does this properly (code "AUTH_REJECTED" vs prose "session limit"); this one does not.

verdict.reason: Verified in-repo. isCredentialRejected (ask.mjs:600-605) checks `if (err.code) return err.code === "AUTH_REJECTED"` then falls back to Number(err.status) === 401/403 — `detail` is never read (contrast isAccountLimit:570-571, which does have a prose fallback). The test at ask.test.mjs:274 asserts `isCredentialRejected({ kind: "api-error", code: "USAGE_LIMIT", detail: "401" }) === false` under a comment claiming "`code` wins over prose", but the fixture carries no `status`, so with line 602 deleted the fallback yields Number(undefined) = NaN and the expression is still false — the assertion cannot fail on the property it claims to prove; `detail: "401"` is inert. The discriminating case (`code` conflicting with a rejecting `status`, e.g. `{ code: "USAGE_LIMIT", status: 401 }` → must be false) appears nowhere: the only fixtures carrying both fields are ask.test.mjs:287 and :297, where code AUTH_REJECTED and status 401 agree, so they cannot detect a non-exclusive code check. The mutant `if (err.code === "AUTH_REJECTED") return true;` (falling through to status instead of returning exclusively) survives the entire suite. Partial mitigation: ask.test.mjs:268 (`{ code: "AUTH_REJECTED", detail: "<REDACTED>" }`, no status) would fail if line 602 were removed outright, so the code branch is not wholly uncovered — but that guards a different mutant, not the precedence property, and is not sufficient to refute. The sibling isAccountLimit test at ask.test.mjs:697 does test exclusivity properly (`{ code: "AUTH_REJECTED", detail: "session limit" }` → false), confirming the asymmetry the finding describes. Vacuous assertion presented as coverage is squarely in the test-adequacy lane.

finding.evidence: The diff exports `SESSION_LIMIT_RE` from redact.mjs and imports it in ask.mjs and auth-smoke.mjs, arguing that duplicated copies drift. metrics.mjs:878 still holds the OLD literal `/\b(?:session|usage)\s+limit\b/i` (with a `code === "USAGE_LIMIT"` preference) and was neither updated nor imported from. No test in metrics.test.mjs exercises a weekly/daily/monthly limit through `classifyFixResult`/`renderFixEffort` — metrics.test.mjs:796 and :840 only use "You've hit your session limit". So the pre-vocabulary (`detail`-only) branch there still misses a weekly window and nothing would catch it.

verdict.reason: The metrics surface's usage-limit behavior IS covered for the new billing periods, just not by a test containing the word "weekly" in metrics.test.mjs. renderFixEffort decides `sessionLimited` from `outcome.code === "USAGE_LIMIT"` first (metrics.mjs:878), and every failure record carries `code` because safeFailure() attaches classifyInfraError's code (ask.mjs:322-328) and all three failure arms of classifyResult spread it (ask.mjs:369-376, 386, 388-394), with classifyFixResult delegating failures to classifyResult (metrics.mjs:831-838). classifyInfraError is the single home of the widened SESSION_LIMIT_RE (redact.mjs:305, 393). So the weekly path is guarded by two real, non-mocked tests in composition: redact.test.mjs:167-169 asserts weekly/daily/monthly details classify as USAGE_LIMIT, and metrics.test.mjs:787-810 drives an actual 429 through classifyFixResult -> renderFixEffort and asserts the USAGE_LIMIT branch renders "not a defect in the PR"/"after that" and NOT "hard ceiling"/"a human should take a look". ask.test.mjs:228 and auth-smoke.test.mjs:34 cover the widened vocabulary on the other consumers. The only thing left uncovered for the new words is the pre-vocabulary detail-only fallback, which is unchanged legacy code (.trusted/scripts/agent/metrics.mjs:878 and .trusted/scripts/agent/metrics.test.mjs:787/840 are identical to the current files) and therefore not a new or changed behavior; the "third copy not unified" half is a duplication/correctness concern outside the test-adequacy lane.
